transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 14:30 PT (Zoom)
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Anjali (LucidBio - Head of ML), Tom (LucidBio - Cloud Arch), Sofia (LucidBio - Security)
Summary: POC scoping focused on private network connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region residency requirements, egress inspection constraints, and benchmark success criteria/timeline. Customer expects limited egress to public internet, strong audit trails, and a 2-3 week benchmark window.
-- Optional auto sections present: Notes, Action items, Questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, should we kick off?
[00:05] Anjali: yeah hi thanks, apologies for the slight delay, got pulled into another stand.
[00:08] Maya: no worries, we'll just run through agenda. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, with me is Diego, our SE who will lead the benchmark and network design.
[00:15] Diego: hi all, nice to meet you. Quick run, want to cover connectivity options, success criteria, sample workload sizing, and outline the bench runs.
[00:23] Tom: that's right. we (LucidBio) are trying to keep all inference traffic inside our VPCs in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, and block any direct internet egress except for control-plane calls.
[00:32] Sofia: also need strong audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and SAML SSO for console. SOC2 is a must.
[00:38] Maya: totally understood. we'll map that to our Private offering. quick clarification: do you prefer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink? We want to scope both and show tradeoffs.
[00:46] Anjali: ideally PrivateLink because peering with multiple accounts brings routing headaches, but we want to see cost and latency implications.
[00:54] Diego: noted. for the POC we'll test both. peering is simpler for throughput but has cross-account route table complexity; PrivateLink gives you logical endpoints and tighter egress control since traffic terminates in our customer VPC endpoint, but there's NAT and ENI considerations.
[01:05] Tom: can you walk through what "terminates in our VPC" means in practice? we worry about hairpinning and also outbound egress — we want no public path for inference payloads.
[01:12] Diego: yeah. with PrivateLink we create a service endpoint in our region that you create a VPC endpoint to. traffic flows over AWS backbone — doesn't traverse public internet. There is an ENI in your subnet with private IPs. No public NAT egress required. Peering would be routed via route tables between VPCs; both are private but peering needs route propagation and can complicate multi-account.
[01:30] Sofia: and with PrivateLink do you still need outbound connections from our side for package updates or metrics?
[01:36] Diego: control-plane telemetry to Redwood's control plane will still happen, and we can route that out via a restricted management VPC or a separate egress path. For the data plane of inference we can keep it entirely inside your VPC with PrivateLink. We'll provide a minimal set of egress IP ranges for control-plane callbacks if needed, or we can do a peered management VPC so it's fully private.
[01:53] Anjali: ok good. let's talk success criteria — what measurable goals should we set for the POC?
[01:58] Maya: from the commercial side we'll want to prove: (1) functional connectivity with PrivateLink/VPC peering, (2) security posture — KMS integration + audit logs, (3) latency and throughput benchmarks that match your SLA targets, and (4) a sizing estimate for dedicated capacity or host config.
[02:12] Diego: to be specific we'll run three benchmark types: baseline latency (p50/p95), throughput saturation (RPS to failure/queuing), and cache-hit performance (KV/prefix cache impact on token cost).
[02:25] Tom: what numbers should we test to? Our internal SLA target is p50 < 300ms and p95 < 1s for a 512-token average payload. Our expected peak is 50 RPS with occasional spikes to 80 for short bursts.
[02:36] Anjali: token lengths vary, but average is 300 tokens, 512 is an upper percentile. cost is also important — we need an estimate of tokens/sec cost for both hosted and dedicated options.
[02:45] Diego: ok, so we'll run with default test vectors: 300 token average, 512 token heavy path, 50 RPS steady-state and 80 RPS burst. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/second throughput, GPU util, and cost estimate. We'll include quantized model variant tests and safety net fallbacks.
[02:58] Sofia: can you also demonstrate that audit logs capture request metadata without storing PII? compliance can't accept raw user data in logs.
[03:05] Diego: yes we can mask payloads in logs and send only non-sensitive metadata. We'll show log redaction in the demo runbook.
[03:12] Maya: timeline wise, customer wants a 2–3 week POC. Step 1: network setup and ACLs (3-4 days), Step 2: bench runs (1 week), Step 3: analysis and readout (2-3 days). That fit?
[03:23] Tom: sounds good. we have security review meetings on 9/2, so kickoff before then would be ideal.
[03:28] Maya: propose 9/8 for pilot kickoff — Diego can you do earlier if we need to?
[03:31] Diego: I can do 9/1 as a backup but need to lock in infra support.
[03:35] Anjali: can you also provide an offline checklist for IAM roles and RBAC? we don't want surprises during setup.
[03:40] Diego: yes, we'll include CloudFormation snippets and IAM least-privilege roles, plus step-by-step for endpoint creation.
[03:46] Tom: about egress: we have strict DLP that inspects egress to external networks. If control-plane IPs are needed, they'll need to be in allowlist form and we need stable ranges. Are your control-plane IPs fixed?
[03:57] Maya: we can provide a published list for the pilot; long term we offer Private options with no public egress or a peered management VPC. We'll include a CIDR list for the POC.
[04:06] Sofia: and what about key management — we need KMS integration so keys are customer-managed; we won't allow Redwood to hold raw keys.
[04:13] Diego: we support BYOK via KMS. For Private we can set up a customer KMS key policy so that encryption/decryption operations are only allowed with your key. We'll document the steps.
[04:22] Anjali: great. on benchmarks: we also want a dataset-level quality check — ensure outputs don't regress with quantized variants. can you run generation quality A/B on 1000 prompts?
[04:30] Diego: yes, we'll run evals and attach redwood optimize recommendations; we'll produce a quality delta table (BLEU/ROUGE or custom metrics) and human spot checks. We'll avoid large exports of customer prompts; keep evals inside your VPC where possible.
[04:43] Tom: any limitations to running in eu-west-1? we need regional lock for EU data residency for some datasets.
[04:50] Diego: we can deploy inference nodes in eu-west-1. PrivateLink and peering both supported regionally. We'll ensure model artifacts and logs for that workflow remain in-region. Some control-plane functions might still be global but we'll publish a flow that minimizes cross-border data.
[05:03] Maya: question from our side: does the customer want Redwood-managed model hosting (we serve the model) or bring-your-own-model container?
[05:11] Anjali: we prefer Redwood to host curated models but need the option to bring our proprietary model later. for the POC start with public model to validate infra.
[05:18] Diego: ok we'll spin up a verified open model and run the quantized variant for cost numbers.
[05:22] Sofia: send over the security questionnaire after call. We'll need network diagrams, SOC2 report, pen test summary.
[05:29] Maya: yes, we'll attach those.
[05:31] Diego: on bench specifics — we'll do three phases: (A) correctness and connectivity smoke tests, (B) steady-state throughput for 50 RPS for 2 hours, measuring tail latency and GPU mem, and (C) spike test to 80 RPS for 10 minutes to observe fallback & autoscaling. We'll also test prefix/KV cache hit rates at 0/50/80 percent to show cost delta.
[05:52] Tom: can you simulate our batching pattern? we occasionally have bursts that benefit from micro-batching.
[05:56] Diego: yes we'll parameterize batch size and latency SLOs in the scripts. We'll also test no-batching low-latency path vs heavy-batch high-throughput path.
[06:05] Anjali: what instrumentation will you expose? we want token-level cost, per-request trace IDs, and per-model route metrics.
[06:12] Diego: Redwood console will show token breakdown, p50/p95, per-model cost; we'll also attach trace IDs to spans for your tracing system (we support OpenTelemetry).
[06:20] Sofia: about logs retention — by default how long do you keep request logs? we need a minimum retention for audits, but also need auto-purge for PII after 30 days.
[06:29] Diego: default is 90 days but for POC we can configure 30-day retention and redaction; production options include long-term audit export to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
[06:38] Maya: any blockers you foresee?
[06:40] Tom: our main blocker is the security team's need for fixed IPs for control-plane allowlisting. If you can't provide stable ranges for the POC they'll want more time.
[06:49] Maya: we'll provide a best-effort CIDR set and propose a peered management VPC if needed.
[06:54] Anjali: one more thing — we want a simple success checklist for the POC: connectivity validated, latency/throughput targets met, KMS and audit logs validated, and a sizing recommendation plus cost estimate.
[07:06] Diego: agreed. we'll produce a one-page POC acceptance criteria doc with pass/fail for each item.
[07:12] Sofia: good. what about pricing for the pilot? are there credits or trial terms?
[07:17] Maya: we typically offer pilot credits for 2–3 weeks; Diego can put together a sample estimate.
[07:22] Diego: I'll include an estimated cost range for hosted vs dedicated reserved baseline for the projected workload.
[07:27] [pause, cross talk]
[07:30] Anjali: ok final check — timeline recap?
[07:33] Maya: propose kickoff 2026-09-08, network setup 3–4 days, bench 1 week, analysis 2–3 days, final readout 2026-09-24. Can you confirm by 2026-09-01?
[07:44] Tom: yes we'll aim to confirm.
[07:46] Sofia: security meeting on 9/2, if they greenlight, we can do 9/8.
[07:50] Maya: great. I'll send the packet and runbook today. Diego will follow up with bench scripts and sizing.
[07:56] Diego: action items: share CFN snippets, sample load scripts, and benchmark templates; also capture the PrivateLink vs peering pros/cons doc.
[08:06] Anjali: and we'll provide a list of sample prompts for the quality evals and confirm regional constraints.
[08:12] Maya: awesome. thanks everyone. we'll recap in the calendar invite and attach docs.
[08:16] Tom: thanks all.
[08:18] Sofia: thanks.
[08:20] End of call.

- Will PrivateLink fully eliminate public egress? (Answer: yes for data plane; control plane needs allowlist or peered management VPC.)
